source_reference: ITU AI Readiness Report 2.0, §2, p12-13 (F2-2-ai-policy-dimension / basic framework table)
implemented_capability: Standardised chunk metadata with provenance, plus typed JSON APIs
evidence: 56 chunks, each with source_id, section, page, jurisdiction, classification, sha256
limitations: Single internal schema; not mapped to FHIR/OMOP or any national data standard.

implemented_capability: Provenance verification, claim classification, append-only audit chain
evidence: 56/56 quotations machine-verified against official sources; hash-chained audit log
limitations: Governance is bounded to the prototype's own corpus and records; no enterprise data governance process.

implemented_capability: Public source retrieval with documented licensing boundaries; no redistribution of restricted documents
evidence: source register records official URLs, licence notes and verification status for 13 sources
limitations: Full texts are fetched to a local cache and not redistributed; offline use therefore degrades to the verified excerpts.

implemented_capability: Single-container deployment; no GPU, no external model API; deterministic offline operation
evidence: Application runs with FastAPI + SQLite and a static React build
limitations: Infrastructure readiness is not claimed; this is a laptop-scale prototype.

implemented_capability: No dependency on connectivity for core workflow
evidence: Retrieval and evaluation run with the network disabled
limitations: Source re-verification does require network access.

implemented_capability: Typed agent contracts, documented scoping, testable orchestration
evidence: 129 backend tests covering invariants, agents, retrieval, the advisory guard, API and scenarios
limitations: Skills readiness of an adopting facility is not assessed.

source_reference: Report 2.0 §2 (Innovation Ecosystem indices include open source)
implemented_capability: MIT-licensed source; no proprietary dependency; vendored standards excerpts kept minimal
evidence: All code is in this repository under MIT; third-party text is quoted minimally
limitations: No community governance, contribution process or release pipeline.

implemented_capability: Explicit mapping to ITU-T Y.3172 concepts and to HL7 FHIR Task / IHE XDW comparators
evidence: Mapping table with code locations, tests and limitations; no conformance claim
limitations: Mapping is interpretive. No conformance testing against Y.3172 or FHIR was performed.

implemented_capability: Jurisdiction-scoped evidence, classification of binding vs guidance vs comparator, human approval gate
evidence: Every consequential action carries either a verified citation or a declared design control
limitations: Policy coverage is limited to the reviewed corpus; it is not a compliance product.

implemented_capability: Configurable institutional profile with labelled design controls; no invented statutory clock
evidence: Clock and escalation values carry PRODUCT_DESIGN_CONTROL labels and gap references
limitations: The facility has not reviewed or approved any profile value.

implemented_capability: Synthetic-only test sandbox with seeded scenarios, replay and audit export
evidence: 28 runs across 7 scenarios; replay signature comparison
limitations: This is an internal test harness, not participation in a regulatory sandbox. 'Sandbox' in the reviewed framework means a supervised environment sanctioned by a regulator, which this is not.

source_reference: Report 2.0 (human interaction theme); Y.3172 human supervision
implemented_capability: Named supervisor role in the workflow; approval-gated corrected-result communication; escalation queue
evidence: Approval required before a correction is re-communicated; withheld actions recorded
limitations: Supervision is simulated. There is no authenticated supervisor identity, so the role is a field in a record rather than a person who can be held to account - the oversight is structural, not attributable, which is why this row is PARTIAL and not IMPLEMENTED.

implemented_capability: Nothing implemented beyond language-neutral message templates and channel-agnostic design
evidence: n/a
limitations: Accessibility, language and low-literacy considerations are not implemented. The Arabic/English wording of a real patient message would need clinical and cultural review.

implemented_capability: No generative model is invoked. The advisory boundary is implemented and tested: a model may propose, is refused if offshore or ungrounded, and can never change a gate decision
code_location: backend/app/advisers/ (base, residency, guard, stub) ; backend/app/orchestration/gate.py::enforce (advisory attached after the decision)
evidence: 15 adviser tests including one that asserts the gate decision is byte-identical with and without an accepted proposal; the boundary is closed by default (enable_llm=False)
limitations: No model client is implemented, by design: the only adviser is a deterministic stub used to exercise containment. Generative-AI behaviour is therefore untested - what is tested is the guard.

implemented_capability: The applicable-instrument decision is explicit: health data is taken out of the PDPL and grounded in the ICT Health Law, which is cited for confidentiality (Art. 4), permitted circulation (Art. 16) and the 25-year retention floor (Art. 20)
evidence: 13 sources, 56 verified excerpts; a Dubai case resolves to {AE-DU, AE-FED} so the federal statute is retrievable and citable, while another emirate and global material stay comparator-only
limitations: Article 13 (no processing of health data outside the State without a Health Authority resolution) is recorded as a binding requirement but the prototype has no data-residency enforcement: it would run against whatever model endpoint is configured. Retention (Art. 20) and the patient-feedback duty (§4.9.10) are recorded and NOT implemented - see GR-13 and GR-14.

implemented_capability: Enforced at two boundaries: the advisory guard refuses an offshore endpoint before any data is shaped, and the model client refuses to construct against an endpoint outside the State
evidence: classify() treats .ae and loopback as in-country and everything else as out-of-country; unknown is refused; the client raises PermissionError at construction
limitations: Checks the endpoint string, not traffic: it cannot see DNS, a proxy, or a model bundled into a desktop app. No in-country endpoint is configured in this build, so the control is tested but not exercised live.

source_reference: UAE AI Charter P5 (Transparency) and P7 (Governance and Accountability) - OFFICIAL_GUIDANCE; ITU AI Readiness Report 2.0 (transparency theme)
implemented_capability: Every step is published as ordered artefacts: event, retrieved evidence with claim class, per-agent proposal with derived confidence and its basis, gate conditions and invariant, transition, resulting state
evidence: Traces are generated from the run itself; the page runs any scenario under two configurations side by side and flags citations outside the case jurisdiction
limitations: Artefacts, not reasoning. Raw model chain-of-thought is deliberately not published: it is unverifiable and invites trust in prose over evidence.

framework_index: Non-binding national guidance distinguished from law
source_reference: UAE AI Charter (June 2024) P6 (human oversight) and P12 (defers to sectoral law) - OFFICIAL_GUIDANCE; UAE AI Strategy 2031 (U5)
implemented_capability: Every excerpt carries a claim class; guidance-class material can inform retrieval and explanation but can never satisfy a binding condition or authorise a fallback channel
evidence: U5 excerpts are classified OFFICIAL_GUIDANCE; ingestion refuses an authorisation declaration from guidance or comparator class
limitations: Classification is authored per excerpt. Nothing machine-checks that a document really is guidance rather than law, so the class is only as good as the source review behind it.

framework_index: Integrity and tamper-evidence of the decision record
source_reference: DoH ADHICS V2/2024 §2.30 (data must not be altered or destroyed in an unauthorised manner) - binding in Abu Dhabi, comparator for Dubai
implemented_capability: Append-only hash-chained audit log, revision lineage, and a reconciliation endpoint that replays persisted transitions against the stored state
evidence: Editing, deleting or reordering an entry breaks verification; divergence between store and replay is reported, never repaired
limitations: Tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: an attacker with write access can rewrite the whole chain. No external anchoring or witness.

framework_index: Patient access to, and correction of, their record
source_reference: Federal Law 2/2019 Art. 5 and 6 (U1); DHA HISHD/PP-08 §4.5.1, §4.9.10 (U4) - right to view and request correction
implemented_capability: Nothing. The system models the provider's communication duty and a patient's acknowledgment, but no patient-facing route exists to inspect or contest the record.
evidence: Searched the corpus and the routes: no endpoint, page or scenario implements a patient access or correction request
limitations: A real deployment would need this before any patient-facing use. Recorded as absent rather than mapped to an adjacent feature.
